basis: GCH1/BH4 synthesis defect causes dystonia; structural pes cavus occurs in 2/4 patients (50%), supporting musculoskeletal involvement with limited precision.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: documented pes cavus is a structural foot deformity in 2/4 patients (50%); the supplied frequency meets the threshold despite the small cohort.

basis: Disseminated TB with defining pulmonary micronodules; hepatic inflammation with biochemical dysfunction occurs in roughly half. Secondary anemia alone does not establish marrow damage.

decisions.haematologic: none: anemia is often secondary to systemic inflammation; direct marrow or functionally significant splenic damage is not established in at least 30%.

basis: Diffuse gastrointestinal polyposis; intellectual disability and vascular hemangiomas are each frequent (30-79%). Blood-loss anemia is secondary.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: hemangiomas are vascular proliferative lesions, meeting direct occupation; HPO reports them in 30-79%, independently of occasional cardiac malformations.

basis: Erythrocyte glutathione synthesis deficiency causes hemolysis. Oxoprolinuria and neurologic annotations conflict with this restricted subtype and suggest generalized disease.

decisions.neurologic: none: intellectual disability in 2/4 accompanies contradictory oxoprolinuria annotations; these do not reliably describe the erythrocyte-restricted, non-oxoprolinuric subtype.

basis: Muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; cleft palate directly affects oral structure in 1/3 reported patients (33%), with limited precision.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate is a structural oral malformation reported in 1/3 patients (33%); the supplied frequency meets the threshold, although the cohort is small.

basis: Biotin deficiency commonly causes encephalopathy, seizures or neuropathy and persistent dermatitis/alopecia; approximately >=30% each in clinically manifest disease, varying by cause.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurologic dysfunction is a characteristic manifestation across inherited and acquired clinical biotin deficiency, estimated at >=30%; psychiatric symptoms alone do not qualify.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent dermatitis and alopecia are characteristic direct manifestations of clinical biotin deficiency, estimated at >=30% across its usual symptomatic course.

basis: Defined by mitochondrial complex III deficiency due to UQCRQ; severe intellectual disability, dystonia and ataxia occur in 20/20 patients.

decisions.neurologic: involved: direct neurologic dysfunction affects 20/20 patients; the concept is defined by its respiratory-chain defect rather than a neurologic diagnostic criterion.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia defines disease. Respiratory insufficiency is frequent (30-79%) but does not establish direct lung disease; direct airway malacia is occasional (5-29%).

decisions.pulmonary: none: frequent respiratory insufficiency can result from skeletal restriction; direct pulmonary pathology is not established, and laryngotracheomalacia occurs in only 5-29%.

basis: Definition excludes Ancylostoma and Necator, the usual human intestinal hookworms. Remaining animal-associated genera do not establish a consistent intestinal site in humans.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: the restricted definition excludes usual human intestinal hookworms; animal intestinal tropism does not establish gastrointestinal localization in human infection.

basis: OEIS defines bladder exstrophy, bowel/anorectal defects and spinal dysraphism. Associated structural hip, vertebral and limb abnormalities occur in 30-79%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: spinal dysraphism is a defining component of OEIS; frequent myelomeningocele confirms that the spinal defects include neural tissue.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: associated hip, vertebral and limb malformations occur in 30-79%; bladder, bowel and neural spinal defects occupy the three primary slots.
